title: introduce-sku-aware-cost-explorer-and-quant-synthesis-cli
author: Claire Nguyen
release_notes: Add a new CLI tool (redwood cost-explorer) to simulate SKU-level unit economics and autogenerate workload-aware quantization profiles. Backwards-compatible; safe gated rollout behind feature flag.
body:
Motivation: Customers frequently ask for per-SKU/unit-unit visibility and actionable defaults. Teams also struggle to pick quantization profiles that preserve quality for a given SKU’s token distribution. This PR adds a developer-facing CLI and library functions that (1) simulate per-SKU unit economics under multiple batch/cache/quant presets, and (2) synthesize candidate quantization profiles from small workload sketches so operators can adopt conservative defaults quickly.

What this PR does (single-string description): Introduces `redwood cost-explorer` (CLI) and supporting packages under pkg/econ and pkg/quant. The explorer accepts a SKU/workload descriptor (sample rate, seqlength-distribution, latency-slo, model-variant hints) and runs a lightweight simulation combining batching, cache-hit heuristics, and per-token cost curves to produce an economic sensitivity report (median/unit cost, p95 latency, cold-warm break-even). The quant-synthesis component analyzes a small set of representative traces (or a synthetic token histogram) and proposes 2–3 quant profiles (safe, balanced, aggressive) along with estimated quality drift score based on a lightweight calibration runner that uses a subset of eval prompts. The CLI can export profiles as YAML to feed into tenant defaults or the optimizer.

Checklist: 
- [x] core simulator & CLI implementation
- [x] quant synthesis prototype + local calibration runner
- [x] unit tests for econ simulator and quant heuristics
- [x] integration smoke test for CLI end-to-end
- [x] docs and CLI usage examples in docs/cost-explorer.md
- [x] feature-flag gating (enable via ENABLE_COST_EXPLORER env var)
- [x] telemetry hooks (opt-in) for adoption metrics

Implementation notes: 
- pkg/econ/explorer.go: event-driven simulator that stitches together batching logic pulled from the runtime batcher simulation but with simplified latency modeling to be fast and deterministic for CLI runs. Uses per-SKU sample rates to compute amortized KV-cache benefits. 
- pkg/quant/synthesizer.py: small Python module (kept separate for iteration speed) that consumes token histograms and outputs profiles. It also contains a thin calibration harness that runs a subset of prompts through a locally-configured test runtime (mocked in CI) to estimate quality delta. 
- cmd/cost-explorer/main.go: CLI front-end with subcommands `run`, `compare`, and `export`. `run` produces human-readable and JSON reports; `compare` runs two presets and shows delta table; `export` writes YAML profiles consumable by the defaults service. 
- Feature flag: ENABLE_COST_EXPLORER and a runtime gate (redwood.features.EconExplorer) used in init paths.

Testing: Unit tests cover the simulator edge cases (zero-cache, high-latency instances, microburst workloads) and quant-synth basic heuristics. CI includes a CLI smoke step that runs `cost-explorer run --sample synthetic_small` against a mocked runtime. Initial CI run flagged a lint error in pkg/quant/synthesizer.py which was fixed in the follow-up commit.

Rollout plan: Merge behind feature flag. We will (1) dogfood on internal tenants with ENABLE_COST_EXPLORER enabled, (2) gather telemetry for two weeks, and (3) expose CLI to customers via developer docs and an examples repo. Not intended as the canonical autotuner yet — this is a fast-feedback tool to populate safe defaults for the autotune pipeline.

Security & privacy: By default CLI runs offline; when calibration is requested it uses a customer-provided eval set. Telemetry is opt-in and documented. No secrets are emitted in reports.

Related: ENG-3476 (SKU awareness for tenant economics), ENG-3591 (quantization profile automation).

review_comments: Ava Patel: Please add a link to the evaluation prompt set you used for calibration. Also - can the quant harness run in pure-Go for CI? Python dependency increases CI surface area.

Claire Nguyen: Added docs pointer and a minimal synthetic eval set under examples/. We kept the quant prototype in Python to iterate quickly; CI runs it inside a lightweight virtualenv step and we vendor the small dependency list. We can port to Go if we decide to promote to runtime. (response to @Ava)

Diego Márquez: Simulator looks good. Two suggestions: (1) include p99 latency in output, and (2) make the KV cache hit model configurable by a simple decay param.
Action: updated explorer.go to expose p99 and to accept cache_decay param. (implemented)

Samir Shah: Can you add a short note on assumptions/limitations to docs? I want operators to know this is a fast estimator not a full load test.
Claire Nguyen: Added a Limitations section in docs/cost-explorer.md. (implemented)
ci_summary: Initial CI: failed (lint in synthesizer.py). Follow-up commits fixed lint and added a pinned venv step. Full CI now passes: unit tests, linters, and CLI smoke step all green.
merge_commit: h8i9j0k SQUASH: introduce sku-aware cost explorer and quant synthesis CLI
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the quant synthesizer as a Python prototype to accelerate iteration. We expect to upstream a Go reimplementation if the approach proves successful in dogfood. CLI UX and export format follow the schema used by tenant-defaults so importing profiles is straightforward.
examples_usage:
# Run a quick simulation
redwood cost-explorer run --sku examples/sample-skus.yaml --mode balanced --output report.json
# Export a suggested quant profile for tenant defaults
redwood cost-explorer export --sku examples/sample-skus.yaml --profile balanced --out-tier-profile balanced-profile.yaml
changelog_entry: Add cost-explorer CLI to simulate SKU economics and generate conservative quant profiles (feature-flagged).
